fluff.overview: A small mob is little more than an angry handful of civilians, perhaps a dozen or two, armed with makeshift weapons and incendiary grenades scavenged from wherever they can find them. These groups form spontaneously around a grievance, a food shortage, a rumor of government betrayal, or simple desperation. They lack any tactical coordination and scatter quickly when confronted by trained soldiers. Their threat is not in combat power but in what they represent: the first spark of wider unrest. A small mob that disperses today may return tomorrow as a large one, and garrison commanders who ignore the warning signs risk losing control of an entire district.
